Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-119096 (score CVSS 9.8).

The Uncanny Toolkit for LearnDash plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in versions up to, and including, 3.8.2 via the `email` parameter of the `uo_login_action()` function. This is due to a parser-differential flaw in which the plugin's account-verification gate resolves the submitted `email` value using the raw, unsanitized string passed to `get_user_by()`, while the subsequent `wp_signon()` call relies on WordPress core's internal `sanitize_user()` to strip appended junk characters — causing the gate lookup to fail and be skipped entirely while the real account is still resolved and authenticated. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in to unverified or administrator-suspended accounts whose credentials they already possess, obtaining a valid `wordpress_logged_in` session cookie and defeating the plugin's account-approval and account-suspension controls. The nonce required to reach the handler is freely obtainable in the same request from the unauthenticated `ult-refresh-nonce` endpoint, making exploitation trivial for any attacker with network access to the site and knowledge of a target account's credentials.

Score CVSS : 9.8

Type de faiblesse (CWE) : CWE-287

items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-109220 (score CVSS 9.8).

The PDF Invoice for WooCommerce + Drag and Drop Template Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.1 via the 'customer_note' parameter parameter. This is due to insufficient sanitization of the customer_note checkout field, which is inlined verbatim into invoice HTML, entity-decoded back into a live tag by simplehtmldom, reassembled into raw bytes by mPDF, and passed to unserialize() in _getObjAttr without validation. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server. An unauthenticated attacker can trigger the vulnerable code path on a default install by placing an anonymous WooCommerce checkout via the public Store API (POST /wc/store/v1/checkout) using a Direct Bank Transfer or cheque payment method, which automatically transitions the order to 'on-hold' status and fires the plugin's invoice-generation hook.

Score CVSS : 9.8

Type de faiblesse (CWE) : CWE-502

Vulnérabilité critique affectant Palo Alto.

Attackers have chained critical PHP2Shell vulnerabilities with the Fragnesia Linux kernel flaw to gain root access on Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS systems.

The campaign reportedly compromised 24 internet-facing firewalls before reaching an internal firewall management server, bringing the total to 25 compromised systems.

Hunt.io’s investigation cites Dream Research’s campaign analysis and describes a transition from honeypot exploitation to production compromises.

However, the findings do not establish reliable mass exploitation across arbitrary PHP servers, where differing software builds and memory layouts complicate successful attacks.

PHP2Shell comprises CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 , two critical memory-safety vulnerabilities rated CVSS 4.0 9.2. The flaws involve PHP session-upload handling and memory cleanup during out-of-memory conditions, potentially enabling remote code execution in vulnerable configurations.

The attack begins through PHP’s session.upload_progress mechanism, which processes attacker-controlled multipart upload data.

Crafted requests manipulate heap allocations, expose memory addresses needed to bypass address space layout randomization, and forge internal structures that redirect execution to PHP’s system() function.

The malware that topped ESET’s infostealer detections in Latin America in the first half of 2026 is an example of how cybercrime has professionalized

items.body:

items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Schneier on Sec..

Interesting research: “ AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities ” Abstract: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. We show this assumption does not hold under adversarial conditions by constructing backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights, decrypting and executing them only upon receiving a secret trigger. Using digital lockers, these hidden circuits remain provably hard to elicit and interpret under cryptographic assumptions, even given full access to model weights, extending prior work from hiding fixed strings to arbitrary computations. We implement our proof of concept constructions in PyTorch and evaluate elicitation through fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training, using a small chemical reaction prediction task as a proxy for CBRN-relevant capabilities. Our results demonstrate resistance to these methods and, together with our cryptographic guarantees, reveal a limit of elicitation-based capability audits. We release our models to support the improvement of defenses.

The company, billing itself as “the next-generation fashion retailer for Millennial and Generation Z consumers,” said a recent hack exposed customer payment card numbers.

Online fashion retailer Revolve warned investors that cybercriminals gained access to payment card numbers and expiration dates during a recent cyber incident.

Revolve did not respond to questions about when the attack occurred but said in the report that an initial investigation found that the threat actors used “automated means” to obtain names, contact information, payment card numbers and payment card expiration dates from customers who saved payment information in their online shopping account on Revolve’s e-commerce platform.

Revolve said it has notified federal law enforcement agencies about the attack and has hired a cybersecurity firm to lead the recovery effort. There were no operational disruptions caused by the attack, and Revolve said it will not face material financial impacts as a result of the incident.

Signal de veille — SANS ISC.

Recently, I had to extract embedded files from a set of OneNote files (extension .one). My onedump.py tool can extract individual files, so I would have to run this many times. To avoid this, I added a new feature to my onedump.py tool: producing JSON data. Several of my tools already have such a feature : they produce JSON data with the content of their analysis results. onedump's option --jsonoutput produces JSON output with the content of each embedded file found inside the OneNote file. And it can do this for many .one files in one go: onedump.py --jsonoutput *.one To write these files to disk you can use my myjson-filter.py tool, like this: onedump.py --jsonoutput *.one | myjson-filter.py -W hashvir This will write all the embedded files to disk, their name will be the sha256 hash of their content plus extension .vir (hashvir).   Didier Stevens Senior handler blog.DidierStevens.com (c) SANS Internet Storm Center. https://isc.sans.edu Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 3.0 United States License.

CISA’s new strategy, CISA 2030, will focus on rapid detection and response and resiliency of critical services ahead of “passive defense”

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency (CISA) has promised to move away from “passive defense” and towards an “aggressive, anticipatory” approach to cyber-threats affecting critical infrastructure.

This was the message of CISA’s new strategy document, CISA 2030: Defend, Harden, Prevail , published on October 26.

The agency provided details on how it will adopt a proactive stance when defending critical infrastructure, including responding to threats faster and building resilient systems.

Nick Anderson, acting director of CISA, wrote in the new CISA document: “The threat landscape we face today is not static. Nation-state actors and other malicious adversaries continue to grow more sophisticated in their efforts to compromise our networks, and there is no guarantee that a strong defense will eliminate intrusions.”

He added: “As President Trump has reminded us, resilience must be the foundation of our approach. We must ensure that when adversaries gain a foothold, we are prepared to detect them quickly, evict them decisively, and keep critical operations running without interruption.”

The strategy is designed to execute recent White House policy announcements around cybersecurity.

Signal de veille — The Register.

General Motors is taking what looks like a light slap on the wrist from a coalition of 35 states and the District of Columbia after agreeing to settle allegations that it collected drivers' data without proper consent and sold it to data brokers that supplied insurance companies. The Washington state AG's office said on Thursday that GM had reached a $220 million settlement with 36 attorneys general over the automaker's collection and sharing of driving data, including precise location information, speed, seatbelt use, and other metrics. According to investigators, GM sold that data to brokers, which in turn supplied it to insurance companies that could use it to set customers' premiums, without drivers' informed consent. For reference, the $220 million settlement, which will be distributed among the participating jurisdictions, equates to less than 7 percent of GM's $3.3 billion in net income attributable to stockholders for its third quarter, which ended on September 30, 2026. Don't spend it all in one place, y'all. The settlement comes more than two years after a 2024 New York Times investigation found that GM had been selling the data collected from vehicle owners through its Smart Driver program. That program, part of GM subsidiary OnStar’s offering, collected the aforementioned data and handed it back to vehicle owners in reports designed to inform better driving habits.

Montant : 0,055 € par Go . L’Arcep estimant à 200 milliards de Go par an le trafic de données expédiées vers les FAI en France, on en arrive effectivement à un rendement potentiel d’environ 10 Md€. Les FAI comme intermédiaires techniques Les FAI feraient office d’intermédiaires pour la collecte d’informations. D’une part, les volumes de données transitant vers leurs clients (ménages et entreprises). De l’autre, l’identification des émetteurs. L’ensemble ferait l’objet d’une transmission trimestrielle à la DGFiP. « La majorité de cette taxe serait acquittée par les grands acteurs internationaux de la tech et du digital », précisent les porteurs de l’amendement. Ils en mentionnent 5 (Google, Meta, Amazon, Netflix Akamai), qui représentent la moitié du trafic relevé par l’Arcep. Un autre argument est d’ordre écologique. La taxe « amènera naturellement […] » à compresser et à optimiser les volumes de données à transmettre.
